timeRange.note: PBDB dates the Chinle occurrences of C. bauri only to stage (Norian to Rhaetian); the Ma values are the ICS v2024/12 stage boundaries. The NHM Dino Directory gives 225-190 Ma for the genus, which includes material from southern Africa not assigned to C. bauri here.

massKg.note: Single published estimate (NHM Dino Directory); method not stated.

summary.en: Coelophysis was a slim, fast meat eater about 2 metres long that lived in the Late Triassic of what is now the United States. Its name means 'hollow form', after its hollow limb bones, which kept it light and agile. It relied on speed, sharp teeth and grasping claws to catch insects and small reptiles. It is one of the early dinosaurs that lived before dinosaurs ruled the land.

text.en: Bones once thought to be baby Coelophysis inside an adult's ribcage, taken as a sign of cannibalism, turned out to belong to a small crocodile relative.
